problems.title: A change of base simplifies a logarithmic equation
problems.question: Solve $\log_3(3x-20)-\log_3(2x-19)=\log_{\sqrt3}\sqrt x$.
problems.idea: Use the standard formula with all domain, orientation and geometric conditions checked.
steps: The logarithm domains require $x>19/2$. Combine the left side and use injectivity to get $(3x-20)/(2x-19)=x$.
This gives $2x^2-22x+20=2(x-1)(x-10)=0$. Only 10 satisfies the domain.

problems.title: A cone with a crossed-out perpendicularity condition
problems.question: A cone generator makes $45^\circ$ with the base plane. Chord $AB=6$, and its distance from the base centre is 4. Find the lateral area using the source with the crossed-out condition omitted.
problems.idea: Use the standard formula with all domain, orientation and geometric conditions checked.
steps: The chord data give $R=\sqrt{16+9}=5$. Then $h=5$ and $l=5\sqrt2$.
The lateral area is $\pi(5)(5\sqrt2)=25\sqrt2\pi$.

If the crossed-out phrase saying MA and MB are perpendicular is retained, triangle MAB would be right with equal sides l. But $AB^2=36$ while $MA^2+MB^2=100$, so that extra condition contradicts the rest.
problems.note: The source visibly crosses out the perpendicular-generator phrase. Reading it as an active condition makes the problem inconsistent; both interpretations are made explicit.

problems.title: A logarithm in an exponential inequality
problems.question: Solve $(0.11)^{\log_2((3x-2)/(4x-1))}<1$.
problems.idea: Use the standard formula with all domain, orientation and geometric conditions checked.
steps: Require $(3x-2)/(4x-1)>1$, which automatically makes the logarithm argument positive.
Subtract 1 to obtain $(-x-1)/(4x-1)>0$. A sign chart with critical values $-1,1/4$ gives $-1<x<1/4$.

problems.title: Two limits obtained by rationalization
problems.question: Evaluate (a) $\lim_{x\to3}(x^2-9)/(\sqrt{x+1}-2)$; (b) $\lim_{x\to\infty}(\sqrt{x^2+x}-\sqrt{x^2-x})$.
problems.idea: Use the standard formula with all domain, orientation and geometric conditions checked.
formulas: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate.
steps: (a) Cancelling $x-3$ after rationalization gives $(x+3)(\sqrt{x+1}+2)$, whose limit is $6\cdot4=24$.
(b) Rationalization gives $2x/(\sqrt{x^2+x}+\sqrt{x^2-x})$. Divide by positive $x$ to obtain $2/(\sqrt{1+1/x}+\sqrt{1-1/x})\to1$.

problems.title: Two derivative calculations
problems.question: $f(x)=x^2\sin3x$, $g(x)=\ln(x+\sqrt{3+x^2})$. Find $f\prime(x)$ and $g\prime(1)$.
problems.idea: Use the standard formula with all domain, orientation and geometric conditions checked.
formulas: Product rule, chain rule and $(\ln u)\prime=u\prime/u$.
steps: $f\prime(x)=2x\sin3x+3x^2\cos3x$.
$g\prime(x)=[1+x/\sqrt{x^2+3}]/[x+\sqrt{x^2+3}]=1/\sqrt{x^2+3}$. Thus $g\prime(1)=1/2$.

problems.title: A pyramid inside a cylinder with square axial sections
problems.question: Two perpendicular axial sections $ABCD,EFKL$ of a cylinder are squares. Find the volume ratio of pyramid $AELKF$ to the cylinder.
problems.idea: Use the standard formula with all domain, orientation and geometric conditions checked.
formulas: Cylindrical height $h=2R$; pyramid volume $=Bh/3$; cylinder volume $=\pi R^2h$.
steps: The pyramid base $ELKF$ is an axial square of area $4R^2$. Since the two section planes are perpendicular, the distance of vertex $A$ from the other section plane is $R$.
The pyramid volume is $4R^3/3$ and cylinder volume $2\pi R^3$. Their ratio is $2/(3\pi)$.

problems.title: A right angle between spatial displacement vectors
problems.question: $A=(1,2,3),B=(-1,1,2),C=(0,3,-2)$. Find $\cos ABC$.
problems.idea: Use the standard formula with all domain, orientation and geometric conditions checked.
formulas: Use vectors $BA,BC$ and the dot-product cosine formula.
steps: $BA=(2,1,1)$ and $BC=(1,2,-4)$. Their dot product is $2+2-4=0$, and both vectors are nonzero.
The angle is right, so its cosine is zero.

problems.title: Construct functions with prescribed limits
problems.question: Give functions with $\lim_{x\to0}xf(x)=2$ and $\lim_{x\to2}g(x)/(x-2)=4$.
problems.idea: Use the standard formula with all domain, orientation and geometric conditions checked.
formulas: A limit does not require the limiting expression to be defined at the approached point.
steps: Choose $f(x)=2/x$ for $x\ne0$ and, if a value at zero is wanted, set $f(0)=0$. Then $xf(x)=2$ off zero.
Choose $g(x)=4(x-2)$. Its quotient by $x-2$ equals 4 off 2. Both limits follow immediately.

problems.title: An angle between skew lines in a rectangular box
problems.question: $AB=2,BC=4,AA_1=6$ and $M$ is midpoint of $A_1B_1$. Find the angle between $BM,DC_1$.
problems.idea: Use the standard formula with all domain, orientation and geometric conditions checked.
formulas: The smaller line-angle cosine is the absolute dot product divided by the length product.
steps: The dot product is 34, and the length product is $\sqrt{37}\sqrt{40}=2\sqrt{370}$.

problems.title: Construct an orthogonal triple of vectors
problems.question: Given $a=(1,-1,2)$, find one nonzero pair $b,c$ such that all three vectors are pairwise perpendicular.
problems.idea: Use the standard formula with all domain, orientation and geometric conditions checked.
formulas: Two nonzero vectors are perpendicular iff their dot product is zero.
steps: Check $a\cdot b=1-1=0$, $a\cdot c=-1-1+2=0$, and $b\cdot c=-1+1=0$.
